test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held On: 28 June, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
A spherical ball of diameter 8 cm is cut into two equal parts. The curved area of one such part has to be painted with green colour, while the other part has to be painted with red colour. The bases of both the hemispheres are to be painted with blue colour. The cost of painting with blue is ₹2/cm², while the cost of painting the curved area is ₹3/cm². What will be the cost (in ₹) of painting the hemispheres?

Take π = 3.14
solution:
Given

Radius = 4 cm

The cost of painting with blue is ₹2/cm2

The cost of painting the curved area is ₹3/cm2

Concept

When the sphere is halved, the total surface area gets increased.

The curved surface area of the hemisphere = 2πr2

Calculation

The curved surface area which is painted red and green = 2 * 2πr2

The cost of painting the curved area is ₹3/cm2 = 3 * 2 * 2πr2

⇒ 12πr2

Two new bases of both the hemispheres are to be painted with blue colour = 2 * πr2

The cost of painting with blue is ₹2/cm2 = 2 * 2 * πr2

⇒ 4πr2

The cost (in ₹) of painting the hemispheres = 12πr2 + 4πr2

⇒ 16πr2 → 16 * 3.14 * 16

⇒ ₹803.84

The cost (in ₹) of painting the hemispheres = ₹803.84
